newsitem.title: USA: Coastal Physician ousted CEO controls board.
newsitem.headline: Coastal Physician ousted CEO controls board.

text.p: Coastal Physician Group Inc said on Wednesday that outsted chief executive Steven Scott, who founded the physician-management company, won a proxy battle to regain control of its board of directors.
The results of the proxy contest confirmed preliminary data released earlier this week.
Shareholders cast their votes during Coastal Physician's annual meeting last month.
At the annual meeting, Scott, already on the nine-member board, offered a slate of three directors that would allow him to take control even if just two nominees were elected.
Scott slate members Mitchell Berger and Henry Murphy were elected to the board.
They replaced President and Chief Executive Joseph Piemont and Robert Hatcher.
Piemont, who remains president and chief executive, encouraged teamwork.
"Now is the time for everyone at Coastal to rise together as a team to meet the challenges and pursue the opportunities ahead of us," Piemont said in a statement.
All other top executives remain in place as well, according to Robert Borchert, a company spokesman.
Scott has said he plans to sell the ailing company. He owns 30 percent of the 23.9 million shares outstanding.

Scott was removed as chief executive in May and had waged a widely publicized fight with management since. The spat ensued after Scott led Coastal Physician on an acquisition spree in 1993 that left the company mired in debt.
Coastal Physician's net losses soared to $24.9 million or $1.04 in the second quarter compared with a loss of $10.5 million, or $0.44, in the same year-ago period.
Coastal management blamed Scott for nearly ruining the company, which has lost clients and was selling businesses to pay its debts.
The existing management had also planned a sale of the company, either piecemeal or completely.
